current.text: Rookie. Utah took him with the number 2 pick in the draft.

Experts disagree on his role. The Utah preview projects him as a starter next to Keyonte George, but a September note says he may not start. He may also play short, staggered stints like Lauri Markkanen does.
Minutes and usage on the Jazz are expected to change a lot early in the season.
He shares the ball with Lauri Markkanen, Keyonte George and Jaren Jackson Jr., who already take a lot of usage.
He will not get anything close to his Summer League usage, so his shots and touches will be capped.
In Summer League he averaged 20 points, 5 assists and 5 turnovers. He shot under 40% from the field and 78% from the line on 38% usage, with some explosive games and some bad ones.
Expect poor FG% and turnover problems this season, mostly early. His shooting should get better as the season goes on.
His assists this season are uncertain. He probably will not reach six per game right away, though one expert thinks Utah can get him more assists than he had at Kansas.
Do not draft him inside the top 100. He is close to impossible to return that price, but he is fine as a late pick around 120 or later.
He has a tight range: best case about 76th, worst case about 148th. One expert would take him over AJ Dybantsa in any format.
He is an upside rookie flyer. If his game comes together he could be a top 15 fantasy player.
Utah plans to win this season and is not expected to tank or shut players down late.

durable.text: He is a high-usage scoring guard. He had 30 usage at Kansas with big three-point volume.
His category strengths are steals, blocks for a guard, scoring and three-point volume, with solid rebounds.
One expert rates him near the top of the class as a shooter.
His assist numbers at Kansas were poor, even though he was a good passer in high school.
He shows some athletic limitations at times.
He missed games and played lower minutes in college because of injuries.
He relies on volume scoring, so he is better in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: The market already has him as a late pick: Yahoo rank 115 (value 2 USD, average cost 3.0 USD) and ESPN rank 126 (1 USD, 2.6 USD). In our 144-player auction he fits as a 1 to 3 USD flyer, so spend no more than that, since the experts see no path to top-100 value this season. No category is flagged weak in his projection. Steals (1.2) and points (18.2) are his best areas, while FG% (45.2% on about 14.5 shots) and 2.1 turnovers lean negative, so he fits builds that can absorb some FG% and TO risk. Early in the season, check whether he starts, how many minutes he gets next to George, Markkanen and Jackson Jr., and whether his FG% and turnovers get better.
